concerns.text: FR-008/SC-006 require validation against the INDEPENDENT published therapy-response signature (PMID 32012345). The plan instead derives the signature from GSE138852 responder labels ('therapy-response signature derived from GSE138852 responder vs. non-responder labels'). This changes the validation construct: a label-derived signature from a study dataset is not the independent published gene set, and GSE138852 is also the validation dataset — creating partial circularity the spec's assumption ('derived from a separate cohort and thus provides an unbiased validation set') explicitly guards against. The plan never mentions PMID 32012345 or how the published gene set will be obtained.

scVelo requires spliced/unspliced count layers (loom files), but the plan's data acquisition (Phase 1) downloads generic GEO supplementary files and preprocessing (Phase 2) builds a standard count matrix via Seurat. The plan never states how spliced/unspliced layers will be obtained for these four accessions. If the supplementary files are count matrices only, velocity is impossible regardless of the T004 retry logic — 'layer detection with explicit errors' reports the gap but the plan has no acquisition strategy (e.g., loom files, alevin/velocyto re-processing) to actually satisfy FR-003. This is a feasibility/methodology gap, not just an error-handling path.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase Order table — Phase 6 (power analysis) after Phase 5 (fork-point detection)
concerns.text: FR-011's power analysis is placed AFTER fork-point detection. Power should be assessed on realized cell counts before or at the start of inference so that underpowered analyses are aborted before results are generated and interpreted. Reorder Phase 6 ahead of Phase 5, or state explicitly that Phase 5 outputs are discarded if power is insufficient.

The cross-dataset Spearman correlation is computed on 'top 3 fork-point genes' (spec target ≥0.80). A rank correlation over 3 items has very few possible values and near-zero resolution; the plan should state how ties/pairs across datasets are formed (e.g., correlation over the full ranked gene list with top-3 reported separately) so the ≥0.80 criterion is statistically interpretable rather than trivially unstable.

FR-008 and SC-006 require validation against an INDEPENDENT PUBLISHED therapy-response signature ("the gene set from PMID 32012345") via Fisher's exact test. The plan's Phase 7 instead derives the signature from GSE138852 responder/non-responder labels: "therapy-response signature derived from GSE138852 responder vs. non-responder labels if actually present". No plan element acquires or uses the published PMID 32012345 gene set, so FR-008/SC-006 as written are unbacked. Either add a step to obtain the published signature (with verified-source handling) or kick back to the spec to amend FR-008.

FR-008 and Constitution Principle VI require validation against an INDEPENDENT PUBLISHED therapy-response signature (PMID 32012345 gene set) via Fisher's exact test. The plan instead derives the signature from GSE138852 responder/non-responder labels ('therapy-response signature derived from GSE138852 response labels if available'). A dataset-internal label-derived signature is not the published independent signature the spec and constitution mandate, and the plan never mentions PMID 32012345 or how its gene set will be obtained/verified. The Constitution-Check row for Principle VI claims PASS, but the plan's substitution weakens the predictor/predicted independence the principle exists to protect. Amend Phase 7 to use the published signature (with verified citation per Principle II), keeping dataset labels as a secondary analysis if desired.

The validation signature is derived from GSE138852 responder vs. non-responder labels, but the plan does not state that GSE138852 is EXCLUDED from fork-point-gene discovery. If fork-point genes are discovered in all four datasets (discovery_dataset_ids is plural and includes GSE138852 by default), then enrichment of those genes against a signature computed from differential expression in the SAME dataset is partially circular: highly variable exhaustion-associated genes will appear in both the fork-point list and the response signature for reasons unrelated to the trajectory claim. Specify a discovery/validation split (discover in GSE136103/127465/111075, validate only in GSE138852), or justify same-dataset enrichment.

FR-008 mandates validation against an INDEPENDENT PUBLISHED therapy-response signature (PMID 32012345, 'derived from a separate cohort and thus provides an unbiased validation set'). The plan replaces this with a signature computed from GSE138852's own response labels. This weakens the independence the spec's validation logic depends on (Constitution VI explicitly requires validation against PUBLISHED signatures). Either use the published gene set as the primary enrichment target (with the GSE138852-label signature as secondary), or document why the published set is unavailable and obtain spec-level sign-off on the substitution.

Spearman correlation of timing ranks for the 'top 3' genes is statistically degenerate: with n=3, Spearman takes only a few discrete values and ≥0.80 essentially forces identical ordering. The plan reports it 'as measured' (good), but should note this is a near-tautological check at n=3 and pre-specify the interpretation (e.g., report correlation over all shared fork-point genes, with top-3 as a spec-mandated subset).
